claims.statement_id: Yanagita menyebut watak yamabito: jujur, bersih, berani, keras kepala, gigih, tidak mau kalah, dan pendendam; dengan itu ia menyajikan gambaran yamabito yang kaya.
claims.quote: 山人の性格として，正直，潔癖，剛気，片意地，執着，負けぎらい，復讐心などが備わっていたことをあげていて，豊かな山人像を提示したのである。

claims.statement: Orikuchi held that yamabito include indigenous people but also villagers who went into the mountains and coastal people who migrated to the mountains, without limiting their origin to one thing.
claims.statement_id: Orikuchi Shinobu berpendapat bahwa yamabito mencakup penduduk asli, tetapi juga orang desa yang masuk gunung dan orang pesisir yang pindah ke pegunungan, tanpa membatasi asal-usulnya pada satu hal.
claims.quote: 折口は山人には先住民もいるが，里に住んだ者が山に入り，さらに海岸の民が山地に移住した者によって構成されているとして，その成立を一義的に限定していない。

claims.statement: According to the Britannica International Encyclopedia, they are said to be naked, large-bodied and red-faced; in Tōhoku, Shinshū and Kyūshū it is told that a yamaotoko came to a mountain hut and begged for mochi.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Britannica Internasional, mereka dikatakan telanjang, bertubuh besar, dan berwajah merah; di Tōhoku, Shinshū, dan Kyūshū diceritakan bahwa yamaotoko datang ke pondok gunung dan meminta mochi.
claims.quote: 裸体で体躯が大きく赤ら顔といわれる。東北地方，信州，九州などで山小屋へ山男が来て餅をせがんだという話が伝えられている。

claims.statement: According to Mypedia, yamabito are imagined as descendants of indigenous people, a mountain kami or its servants, or yokai such as oni and tengu; they are also said to be naked red-faced giants who appear in villages asking for salt.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mypedia, yamabito dibayangkan sebagai keturunan penduduk asli, dewa gunung atau pelayannya, atau yokai seperti oni dan tengu; mereka juga dikatakan raksasa telanjang berwajah merah yang muncul di desa meminta garam.
claims.quote: 先住民の子孫，山の神またはその奉仕者，鬼や天狗(てんぐ)などの妖怪と想像されている。赤顔裸体の巨人で，里に現れて塩を求めるともいわれる。

claims.statement: According to Nipponica, the word yamabito already appears in ancient documents, but it is unclear whether it then meant indigenous people; old documents record yamabito going to the capital and serving at court, and the Gōke Shidai (1111) says they performed the niwabi role.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Nipponica, kata yamabito sudah tampak dalam naskah kuno, tetapi tidak jelas apakah ketika itu berarti penduduk asli; naskah lama mencatat yamabito datang ke ibu kota dan mengabdi di istana, dan Gōke Shidai (1111) menyebut mereka bertugas dalam niwabi.
claims.quote: 山人という語は、古代の文献にもみえているが、それが当時においても先住民を意味していたかどうかはよくわからない。古文献によると、山人が都に出て宮廷に仕えた記事もあり、『江家次第(ごうけしだい)』（1111）によると庭燎(にわび)の役を勤めたとある。

claims.statement: Yanagita carried out a large survey of 50 mountain villages across the country over three years from 1934, trying to grasp the reality of the yamabito remaining in the mountains.
claims.statement_id: Yanagita mengadakan survei besar-besaran ke 50 desa pegunungan di seluruh negeri selama tiga tahun sejak 1934 untuk menangkap kenyataan yamabito yang tersisa di gunung.
claims.quote: 柳田は，その山に残った山人の実体をとらえようとして，1934年から3年間をかけて全国50の山村の調査を大々的に行った

claims.statement: Minakata Kumagusu was highly critical of Yanagita's research, heaping severe criticism and ridicule on belief that the Yamabito ever existed.
claims.statement_id: Minakata Kumagusu sangat mengkritik penelitian Yanagita, mencela keyakinan bahwa yamabito pernah ada.
claims.quote: Minakata Kumagusu was highly critical of Yanagita's research, "heaping severe criticism and ridicule on belief that ... the Yamabito ever existed."

claims.statement: According to records, between 1915 and 1916 the two scholars exchanged letters debating the existence of the Yamabito.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan, antara 1915 dan 1916 kedua sarjana itu bertukar surat memperdebatkan keberadaan yamabito.
claims.quote: According to records, between 1915 and 1916, the two scholars exchanged letters debating the existence of the Yamabito.

claims.statement: One of the concepts Yanagita presents in Tono Monogatari is kamikakushi, being literally spirited away.
claims.statement_id: Salah satu konsep yang disajikan Yanagita dalam Tono Monogatari adalah kamikakushi, yaitu "disembunyikan oleh kami".
claims.quote: One of the concepts Yanagita presents in Tono Monogatari is that of, literally, being spirited away, or kamikakushi.

claims.statement: Yashima no Hage-tanuki is a supernatural tanuki from Yashima.
claims.statement_id: Yashima no Hage-tanuki adalah tanuki gaib dari Yashima.
claims.quote: Yashima no Hage-tanuki (屋島の禿狸) is a Bake-danuki (化け狸, Supernatural raccoon dog), who appears in the legends of Yashima, Takamatsu, Kagawa Prefecture.

claims.statement: Tasaburō-tanuki is one of its alternate names.
claims.statement_id: Tasaburō-tanuki adalah salah satu nama lainnya.
claims.quote: He is also called Tasaburō-tanuki (太三郎狸), Yashima no Hage, and Yashima no Kamuro (屋島の禿).

claims.statement: An account makes him the descendant of a wounded tanuki.
claims.statement_id: Satu kisah menjadikannya keturunan tanuki yang terluka.
claims.quote: This wounded tanuki's descendant is said to be Yashima no Hage-tanuki.

claims.statement: He becomes the guardian of Yashima-ji after the Taira clan’s fall.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi pelindung Yashima-ji setelah kejatuhan klan Taira.
claims.quote: After the Taira clan was ruined, Hage-tanuki became the protector deity of Yashima-ji, the 84th temple on the Shikoku 88-temple pilgrimage.

claims.statement: His skill at transformation was called the best in Japan, and he achieved the rank of supreme commander of the tanuki in Shikoku.
claims.statement_id: Kemampuan transformasinya disebut yang terbaik di Jepang, dan ia mencapai pangkat panglima tertinggi para tanuki di Shikoku.
claims.quote: His skill at transformation was called the best in Japan, and he achieved the rank of supreme commander of the tanuki in Shikoku.

claims.statement: In times of extreme cold, 300 tanuki of his household would gather together, and he would show phantom magic to Minamoto no Yoshitsune's Yasō Tobi and Yumi Nagashi, as happened during the Genpei War.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cuaca sangat dingin, 300 tanuki rumah tangganya berkumpul, dan ia memperlihatkan sihir bayangan pada Yasō Tobi dan Yumi Nagashi milik Minamoto no Yoshitsune, seperti terjadi pada Perang Genpei.
claims.quote: In times of extreme cold, 300 tanuki of his household would gather together, and he would show phantom magic to Minamoto no Yoshitsune's Yasō Tobi (八艘飛び) and Yumi Nagashi (弓流し), as happened during the Genpei War.

claims.statement: One story says Hage-tanuki was shot and killed by a hunter; in another version he died in a contest of disguises with Shibaemon-tanuki of Awaji.
claims.statement_id: Satu kisah menyebut Hage-tanuki tewas ditembak pemburu; versi lain menyebut ia mati dalam adu penyamaran melawan Shibaemon-tanuki dari Awaji.
claims.quote: One story of Hage-tanuki's death is that he was shot and killed by a hunter. In another version, he died in a contest of disguises with Shibaemon-tanuki of Awaji.

claims.statement: In the contest, the fleet had been Hage-tanuki's disguise, successfully tricking Shibaemon; when Hage-tanuki praised Shibaemon loudly he was reprimanded by a soldier for insolence and killed by a spear, since it had been the real Daimyo's procession.
claims.statement_id: Dalam adu penyamaran itu, armada kapal perang adalah penyamaran Hage-tanuki yang berhasil menipu Shibaemon; ketika Hage-tanuki memuji Shibaemon dengan lantang, ia ditegur seorang prajurit karena lancang dan dibunuh dengan tombak, sebab arak-arakan itu adalah arak-arakan daimyo yang sebenarnya.
claims.quote: The fleet had been Hage-tanuki's disguise, successfully tricking Shibaemon. ... Hage-tanuki praised Shibaemon in a loud voice, but was reprimanded by a soldier for his insolence and was killed by a spear; it had been the real Daimyo's procession.

claims.statement: After Hage-tanuki's death, his spirit moved to dwell in Awa Province (now Tokushima Prefecture) and started to possess humans.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Hage-tanuki mati, rohnya pindah ke Provinsi Awa (kini Prefektur Tokushima) dan mulai merasuki manusia.
claims.quote: After Hage-tanuki's death, his spirit moved to dwell in Awa Province (now Tokushima Prefecture), and started to possess humans.

claims.statement: In the years of Kaei, in Hayashimura, Awa district, he possessed a female hairdresser, made predictions, and was said to have dropped a tanukitsuki (tanuki possession).
claims.statement_id: Pada tahun-tahun Kaei di Hayashimura, distrik Awa, ia merasuki seorang penata rambut perempuan, membuat ramalan, dan konon menjatuhkan tanukitsuki (kerasukan tanuki).
claims.quote: In the years of Kaei, in Hayashimura, Awa district (now Awa city), he possessed a female hairdresser, made predictions, and was said to have dropped a tanukitsuki (tanuki possession).

claims.statement: After Kinkyō-tanuki and Rokuemon-tanuki killed each other, their offspring were about to take revenge on each other, and Yashima no Hage-tanuki arbitrated between them and settled the issue.
claims.statement_id: Setelah Kinkyō-tanuki dan Rokuemon-tanuki saling membunuh, keturunan mereka hendak saling membalas dendam, tetapi Yashima no Hage-tanuki menengahi dan menyelesaikan masalah itu.
claims.quote: After Kinkyō-tanuki and Rokuemon-tanuki killed each other, their offspring were about to try to take revenge on each other, and Yashima no Hage-tanuki arbitrated between them and settled the issue.

claims.statement: Because he performed many good deeds, in Takamatsu he is now called Minoyama Daimyōjin; he is the god of family happiness, marriage, and the entertainment business, and is believed to bring good fortune to children.
claims.statement_id: Karena banyak perbuatan baiknya, di Takamatsu ia kini disebut Minoyama Daimyōjin; ia dewa kebahagiaan keluarga, pernikahan, dan dunia hiburan, dan dipercaya membawa keberuntungan bagi anak-anak.
claims.quote: Yashima no Hage-tanuki performed many good deeds, so now in Takamatsu he is called Minoyama Daimyōjin (蓑山大明神). He is the god of family happiness, marriage, and the entertainment business; and is believed to bring about good fortune to children.

claims.statement: He is counted as one of the "three famous tanuki of Japan", along with Danzaburou-danuki of Sado and Shibaemon-tanuki of Awaji.
claims.statement_id: Ia dihitung sebagai salah satu dari "tiga tanuki termasyhur Jepang", bersama Danzaburō-danuki dari Sado dan Shibaemon-tanuki dari Awaji.
claims.quote: He is counted as one of the "three famous tanuki of Japan", along with Danzaburou-danuki of Sado and Shibaemon-tanuki of Awaji.

claims.statement: Afterwards, in the First Sino-Japanese and Russo-Japanese wars, Hage-tanuki departed with many of his followers towards Manchuria.
claims.statement_id: Setelah itu, pada Perang Tiongkok-Jepang Pertama dan Perang Rusia-Jepang, Hage-tanuki berangkat bersama banyak pengikutnya ke Manchuria.
claims.quote: Afterwards, in the First Sino-Japanese and Russo-Japanese wars, Hage-tanuki departed with many of his followers towards Manchuria.

claims.statement: According to the Japan Tourism Agency explanation database, the sanctuary is dedicated to Minoyama Daimyojin, a legendary local spirit who took the form of a tanuki but was believed to be able to shape-shift at will, and the deity is said to bring good luck in family life, marriage and the nighttime entertainment business.
claims.statement_id: Menurut basis data penjelasan Badan Pariwisata Jepang, kuil itu dipersembahkan bagi Minoyama Daimyojin, roh lokal legendaris berwujud tanuki yang dipercaya dapat berubah wujud sesuka hati, dan dewa ini dikatakan membawa keberuntungan bagi kehidupan keluarga, pernikahan, dan bisnis hiburan malam.
claims.quote: The sanctuary is dedicated to Minoyama Daimyojin, a legendary local spirit who took the form of a tanuki but was believed to be able to shape-shift at will. The deity is said to bring good luck in family life and marriage, and to the nighttime entertainment business.

claims.statement: The Traditional Chinese text on the same page says the deity enshrined, Minoyama Daimyojin, is named Yashima Tasaburō-tanuki, one of Japan's three famous tanuki, usually appearing in tanuki form and able to change form at will, with transformation ability the best in Japan.
claims.statement_id: Teks bahasa Mandarin tradisional pada halaman yang sama menyebut dewa yang dipuja, Minoyama Daimyojin, bernama Yashima Tasaburō-tanuki, salah satu dari tiga tanuki termasyhur Jepang, yang biasanya tampil sebagai tanuki dan dapat berubah wujud sesuka hati, dengan kemampuan transformasi yang terbaik di Jepang.
claims.quote: 這座小神社供奉的是「蓑山大明神」，衪是傳說中的當地神明，名叫「屋島太三郎狸」，是日本三大名狸之一，平時以狸貓的形象出現，擁有隨意變幻形象的能力，其幻化能力堪稱冠絕日本。

claims.statement: Although Japanese mythology often describes shape-shifting tanuki as mischievous, the story goes that Minoyama Daimyojin helped the priest Kukai (774-835) when he became lost in the mist on Yashima, appearing disguised as an old man in a cloak and guiding him safely to the top of the mountain.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun tanuki pengubah wujud sering digambarkan jahil dalam mitologi Jepang, kisahnya menyebut Minoyama Daimyojin menolong pendeta Kūkai (774-835) yang tersesat dalam kabut di Yashima: dewa itu menjelma menjadi lelaki tua berjubah dan menuntunnya selamat ke puncak gunung.
claims.quote: Although Japanese mythology often describes shape-shifting tanuki as mischievous, the story goes that Minoyama Daimyojin helped the priest Kukai (774–835) when he became lost in the mist on Yashima. The deity appeared to Kukai disguised as an old man in a cloak and guided him safely to the top of the mountain.

claims.statement: A small shrine beside the main hall at Yashimaji, with a tunnel of red torii gates, has an entrance flanked by two large tanuki statues rather than the fox statues usual at an Inari shrine.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kuil kecil di samping aula utama Yashimaji, dengan lorong gerbang torii merah, pintu masuknya dijaga dua patung besar tanuki, bukan patung rubah seperti lazimnya kuil Inari.
claims.quote: A tunnel of red torii gates leads to a small shrine beside the main hall (hondo) at Yashimaji Temple. This type of tunnel usually marks the entrance to an Inari shrine, with fox statues on either side of the path. However, the entrance to this shrine is flanked by two large statues of tanuki (racoon dogs).

claims.statement: According to the database, the legendary tanuki also appeared in the Studio Ghibli animated film Pom Poko (1994).
claims.statement_id: Menurut basis data itu, tanuki legendaris ini juga muncul dalam film animasi Studio Ghibli Pom Poko (1994).
claims.quote: This is just one of several stories involving the legendary tanuki, who also made an appearance in the Studio Ghibli animated film Pom Poko (1994).

claims.statement: In the past, a tanuki wounded by a fatal arrow was saved by Taira no Shigemori; to repay the debt, the tanuki swore to protect the Taira clan, and its descendant is said to be Yashima no Hage-tanuki.
claims.statement_id: Dahulu ada seekor tanuki yang terluka panah maut tetapi diselamatkan Taira no Shigemori; sebagai balas budi, tanuki itu bersumpah melindungi klan Taira, dan keturunannya disebut Yashima no Hage-tanuki.
claims.quote: In the past, there was a tanuki who was wounded by a fatal arrow shot, but was saved by Taira no Shigemori. To pay his debt of gratitude, the tanuki swore to protect the Taira clan. This wounded tanuki's descendant is said to be Yashima no Hage-tanuki.

claims.statement: Yazi is one of the nine sons of the dragon in Chinese tradition.
claims.statement_id: Yazi adalah salah satu dari sembilan putra naga dalam tradisi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: 睚眦（がいさい、拼音：Yázì）は、竜生九子の一つ。ヤマイヌの首をもち、気性が激しく荒く、争いや殺す事を好む。

claims.statement: It has a wild dog’s head.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki kepala anjing liar.
claims.quote: 睚眦（がいさい、拼音：Yázì）は、竜生九子の一つ。ヤマイヌの首をもち、気性が激しく荒く、争いや殺す事を好む。

claims.statement: Its character is fierce and associated with combat.
claims.statement_id: Sifatnya ganas dan dikaitkan dengan pertempuran.
claims.quote: 睚眦（がいさい、拼音：Yázì）は、竜生九子の一つ。ヤマイヌの首をもち、気性が激しく荒く、争いや殺す事を好む。

claims.statement: Its image appears on weapons and military banners.
claims.statement_id: Gambarnya terdapat pada senjata dan panji militer.
claims.quote: よって、刀の環（刀を佩びるための輪）や、剣の鯉口、武器や罪人を処刑するための鎌や矛に彫られ、古代（三国志時代）には軍旗などの図案に多く用いられた。

claims.statement: According to the Shuolue, the nine sons of the dragon are not dragons and each has its own fondness: Yazi likes killing and is used to adorn sword hilts; the others are Qiuniu, Chaofeng, Pulao, Suanni, Baxia, Bi'an, Xixi and Chiwen.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Shuolue, sembilan putra naga bukan naga dan masing-masing punya kegemaran: Yazi gemar membunuh dan dipakai menghiasi gagang pedang; delapan lainnya adalah Qiuniu, Chaofeng, Pulao, Suanni, Baxia, Bi'an, Xixi, dan Chiwen.
claims.quote: 龍生九子，不成龍，各有所好。囚牛，好音樂，以飾胡琴。睚眦，好殺，以飾刀柄。嘲風，好險，在殿角。蒲牢，好鳴，取為鐘紐。狻猊，好座，取為佛座。霸下，好負重，為碑座。狴犴，好訟，為獄門。屓屭，好文，在碑兩傍。蚩吻，好吞，在殿脊。

claims.statement: According to the Shuolue, in the Hongzhi era a palace official asked Li Dongyang for the names of the dragon's nine sons; he could not give them all, Liu Ji obtained them from an old register of unknown origin, and the author judged the account unfounded (bujing).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Shuolue, pada masa Hongzhi seorang pejabat istana bertanya tentang nama kesembilan putra naga kepada Li Dongyang, yang tidak dapat menyebutkannya; Liu Ji lalu mendapatkannya dari sebuah catatan lama yang asal-usulnya tidak diketahui, dan penulis menilai uraian itu tidak berdasar (bujing).
claims.quote: 弘治間，泰陵令中官問龍生九子名目於李少師東陽，李不能悉，詢於吏部劉員外績，乃得其說，於故冊面上所錄，然亦不知所從出，因據以復。余憶十一、二時，曾見其說於《對類總龜》中，近因歴考傳記，乃知其說為不經。

claims.statement: According to the Shuolue, the term 睚眦 appears in the Zhanguoce in a line about the worthy being moved by a slight resentment; the note explains ya as "raising the eyes" and zi as "the eye socket".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Shuolue, istilah 睚眦 muncul dalam Zhanguoce dengan kalimat "Orang berbudi tergerak oleh sedikit kemarahan"; catatannya menjelaskan ya sebagai "mengangkat mata" dan zi sebagai "rongga mata".
claims.quote: 睚眦，《戰國策》聶政曰：賢者以感忿睚眦之意。注：睚，舉眼也；眦，目匡也。

claims.statement: According to Japanese Wikipedia, the character 睚 derives from the edge of the eye and 眦 from the part where the eye just begins to open; both mean the corner of the eye.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, 睚 berasal dari tepi mata dan 眦 dari bagian mata yang baru mulai terbuka; keduanya berarti sudut mata.
claims.quote: 『睚』の字の由来は目のきわ、『眦』は目のわずかに開きはじめた部分、で、どちらも、まなじりや目じりという意味である。

claims.statement: Both characters also mean "to glare"; 睚眦 means to look in anger and, by extension, "slight"; the 睚眦之怨 of the Shiji is a grudge as small as being glared at.
claims.statement_id: Kedua huruf itu juga berarti "melotot"; 睚眦 berarti menatap marah dan, secara luas, "sedikit"; 睚眦之怨 dalam Shiji adalah dendam setingkat dipelototi sedikit.
claims.quote: また、どちらに字にも『にらむ』という意味があり、転じて『睚眦』には『目を怒らして見る。にらむ』という意味があり、転じて『わずか』という意味もある。史記・范雎伝にある『睚眦之怨』（がいさいのうらみ）は、ちょっとにらまれた程度の恨み、という意味である。

claims.statement: Zaō Gongen is a principal sacred figure in Shugendō.
claims.statement_id: Zaō Gongen adalah sosok suci utama dalam Shugendō.
claims.quote: 蔵王権現（ざおうごんげん）は、日本独自の山嶽仏教である修験道の本尊である。正式名称は金剛蔵王権現（こんごうざおうごんげん）、または金剛蔵王菩薩（こんごうざおうぼさつ）。

claims.statement: Kongō Zaō Gongen is a formal name.
claims.statement_id: Kongō Zaō Gongen adalah nama resminya.
claims.quote: 正式名称は金剛蔵王権現（こんごうざおうごんげん）、または金剛蔵王菩薩（こんごうざおうぼさつ）。

claims.statement: A tradition says the figure appeared during En-no-Ozunu’s mountain practice.
claims.statement_id: Satu tradisi menyebut sosok itu muncul ketika En-no-Ozunu berlatih di gunung.
claims.quote: 蔵王権現は、役小角が、吉野の金峯山で修行中に示現したという伝承がある。

claims.statement: Zaō Gongen is regarded as a combination of Shaka Nyorai, Senju Kannon and Miroku Bosatsu, and three nearly identical images are enshrined side by side as principal image in the Zaō-dō at Yoshino.
claims.statement_id: Zaō Gongen dianggap penggabungan Shaka Nyorai, Senju Kannon, dan Miroku Bosatsu, dan tiga arca yang nyaris sama dipuja berdampingan sebagai arca utama di Zaō-dō, Yoshino.
claims.quote: 釈迦如来、千手観音、弥勒菩薩の三尊の合体したものとされ、今でも吉野山の蔵王堂には互いにほとんど同じ姿をした三体の蔵王権現像が並んで本尊として祀られている。

claims.statement: According to the Heibonsha World Encyclopedia, he is a bodhisattva who subdues demonic obstacles, an incarnation of Shakyamuni's wrathful form, said to have been perceived by En no Gyōja, founder of Shugendō, at the summit of Mt. Kinpu after praying for the salvation of beings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Dunia Heibonsha, ia adalah bodhisatwa penakluk rintangan setan, jelmaan murka Buddha Shakya, yang dikatakan dirasakan En no Gyōja, pendiri Shugendō, di puncak Gunung Kinpu setelah berdoa demi menyelamatkan makhluk hidup.
claims.quote: 修験道の開祖役行者（えんのぎようじや）が金峰山（きんぷせん）の頂上で衆生済度のため祈請して感得したと伝える魔障降伏の菩薩で，釈迦仏の教令輪身。

claims.statement: According to the same encyclopedia, his form has one face, three eyes and two arms, with a blue-black body in a wrathful aspect; the left hand forms a sword mudra at the waist, the right holds a three-pronged vajra high overhead, the left foot treads a boulder and the right leaps into the air.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia yang sama, wujudnya berwajah satu bermata tiga berlengan dua, berkulit biru kehitaman dalam rupa murka; tangan kiri membentuk mudra pedang di pinggang, tangan kanan mengangkat vajra bercabang tiga di atas kepala, kaki kiri menginjak batu karang, dan kaki kanan melompat ke udara.
claims.quote: 形像は一面三目二臂（ひ），身色青黒の忿怒形（ふんぬぎよう）で，左手は剣印を結んで腰につけ，右手は三鈷杵（さんこしよ）を奉持して頭上高く掲げ，左足は磐石を踏み，右足は空中に躍らす。

claims.statement: He does not appear in the sutras and ritual manuals; he is a distinctive gongen born within the mountain worship of Japan, apparently derived from the worship of great rocks.
claims.statement_id: Ia tidak tercantum dalam kitab sutra, melainkan gongen khas yang lahir dalam pemujaan gunung Jepang, dan tampaknya berasal dari pemujaan batu besar.
claims.quote: 経軌（きようき）には見えず，日本の山岳信仰の中で生まれた独自の権現で，磐境（いわさか）の巨石信仰に由来すると思われる。

claims.statement: In the mid-Heian period, when Miroku worship flourished, Mt. Kinpu was likened to the inner court of Tusita and Kongō Zaō was regarded as an incarnation of Miroku.
claims.statement_id: Pada pertengahan zaman Heian, ketika pemujaan Maitreya (Miroku) berkembang, Gunung Kinpu disamakan dengan surga Tusita dan Kongō Zaō dianggap penjelmaan Miroku.
claims.quote: 平安中期に弥勒（みろく）信仰が盛んになり，金峰山は弥勒浄土の兜率（とそつ）内院に擬せられ，金剛蔵王は弥勒の化身とされた。

claims.statement: The oldest image is a fine-line engraved mirror image held at Sōjiji (Nishiarai Daishi), Tokyo, a national treasure, made in 1001.
claims.statement_id: Arca tertua adalah cermin berukir halus milik Sōjiji (Nishiarai Daishi), Tokyo, sebuah harta nasional, yang dibuat pada 1001.
claims.quote: 最古の像は東京都総持寺（西新井大師）所蔵の毛彫鏡像（国宝）で，1001年（長保3）の作である。

claims.statement: According to Britannica International, the name Zaō Gongen came into use from the mid-Heian period; the oldest example is the inscription on a sutra cylinder that Fujiwara no Michinaga buried in 1007 at the Mt. Kinpu sutra mound in Yamato.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Britannica Internasional, nama Zaō Gongen dipakai sejak pertengahan zaman Heian; contoh tertuanya adalah tulisan pada tabung sutra yang dikubur Fujiwara no Michinaga pada 1007 di situs kuburan sutra Gunung Kinpu, Yamato.
claims.quote: 蔵王権現というようになったのは平安時代中期頃からで，藤原道長が寛弘4 (1007) 年に大和の金峯山経塚に埋めた経筒の銘文に記されたのが古い例である。

claims.statement: According to Nipponica, in Shugendō people undergo patient discipline on steep mountains to subdue the demons in their hearts and gain power; Zaō Gongen was born from this, not from sutras or ritual manuals.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Nipponica, dalam Shugendō orang menjalani latihan sabar di gunung terjal untuk menaklukkan setan dalam hati dan memperoleh kekuatan; Zaō Gongen lahir dari latihan itu, bukan dari kitab sutra atau tata cara ritual.
claims.quote: 修験道では険峻(けんしゅん)な山で忍苦の行(ぎょう)をし、心中の悪魔を降伏して験力を得ようとするが、そのようななかから生み出されたものであり、経軌(きょうき)（経典や儀軌）によるものではない。

claims.statement: Because the Honchō Hokke Genki tells of the monk Tenjō (d. 849) visiting the presence of Kongō Zaō at Mt. Kinpu in his lifetime, it is certain that he was already enshrined in the early Heian period.
claims.statement_id: Karena Honchō Hokke Genki memuat kisah biksu Tenjō (wafat 849) yang menziarahi hadapan Kongō Zaō di Gunung Kinpu semasa hidup, dapat dipastikan bahwa ia sudah dipuja pada awal zaman Heian.
claims.quote: 《本朝法華験記》に，849年（嘉祥2）に没した僧転乗が生前金峰山の金剛蔵王宝前に参詣した話を載せているので，平安初期に奉斎されていたことは確実である。

claims.statement: According to Nipponica, this is the wrathful demon-subduing image that En no Ozunu is said to have perceived on Mt. Kinpu, Nara Prefecture, after severe discipline; a three-eyed face with bristling hair, right hand brandishing a three-pronged vajra, left hand forming a sword mudra, standing on his left foot alone on a rock.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Nipponica, ini adalah arca murka penakluk setan yang dikatakan dirasakan En no Ozunu di Gunung Kinpu, Prefektur Nara, setelah latihan keras; wajah bermata tiga dengan rambut berdiri, tangan kanan mengayunkan vajra bercabang tiga, tangan kiri membentuk mudra pedang, dan berdiri pada satu kaki kiri di atas batu.
claims.quote: 奈良時代の呪術者(じゅじゅつしゃ)役小角(えんのおづぬ)が、奈良県金峰山(きんぶせん)上で難行苦行ののち、感得したと伝える悪魔降伏(ごうぶく)の忿怒(ふんぬ)相の像。三目の顔で怒髪(どはつ)天をつき、右手は三鈷杵(さんこしょ)を握って高く振り上げ、左手は剣印を結んで腰部に当て、右足を振り上げ、左足のみにて岩石上に立つ形をとる。

claims.statement: According to Japanese Wikipedia, the right-hand vajra shows crushing heavenly demons, the left-hand sword mudra a sharp blade cutting off all desire and afflictions, the left foot treading holds down demons underground, the raised right foot sweeps away demons between heaven and earth, and the flames behind represent great wisdom.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, vajra tangan kanan melambangkan penghancuran iblis langit, mudra pedang tangan kiri pedang tajam yang memutus nafsu dan kekotoran batin, injakan kaki kiri menekan iblis di bawah tanah, tendangan kaki kanan mengusir iblis antara langit dan bumi, dan api di belakangnya kearifan besar.
claims.quote: 右手の三鈷杵は天魔を粉砕する相を示し、左手の刀印は一切の情欲や煩悩を断ち切る利剣を示す。左足の踏みつけは地下の悪魔を押さえつけており、右足の蹴り上げは天地間の悪魔を払っている姿、背後の炎は大智慧をあらわしている。

claims.statement: In Shinto-Buddhist syncretic teaching he was regarded as the same deity as Emperor Ankan, so at the Meiji-era separation of Shinto and Buddhism many shrines other than Kinpusen-ji made Emperor Ankan their enshrined deity.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ajaran sinkretisme Shinto-Buddha ia dianggap satu dewa dengan Kaisar Ankan, sehingga pada pemisahan Shinto-Buddha zaman Meiji banyak kuil selain Kinpusen-ji menjadikan Kaisar Ankan sebagai dewa utama.
claims.quote: 神仏習合の教説では安閑天皇（広国押建金日命）と同一の神格とされたため、明治時代の神仏分離の際には、本山である金峯山寺以外の蔵王権現を祀っていた神社では祭神を安閑天皇としたところも多い。

claims.statement: In Shinto, Zaō Gongen was syncretized and identified with Kuninotokotachi, Ōnamuchi, Sukunahikona, Yamato Takeru, Kanayamabiko and others, so shrines enshrining him mainly came to worship those five groups of deities.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Shinto, Zaō Gongen disinkretiskan dan disamakan dengan Kuninotokotachi, Ōnamuchi, Sukunahikona, Yamato Takeru, Kanayamabiko, dan lainnya, sehingga kuil yang memujanya terutama memuliakan kelima kelompok dewa tersebut.
claims.quote: また神道において、蔵王権現は国常立尊、大己貴命、少彦名命、日本武尊 、金山毘古命等と習合し、同一視された。その為蔵王権現を祭る神社では、主に上記の5組の神々らを祭神とするようになった。

claims.statement: According to Japanese Wikipedia, "Kongō Zaō" means a king who embodies ultimate indestructible truth and rules over all things, and gongen means a kami or buddha who appears in a provisional form.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia bahasa Jepang, "Kongō Zaō" berarti raja yang mewujudkan kebenaran tertinggi yang tak binasa dan menguasai segala sesuatu, dan gongen berarti dewa-buddha yang tampil dalam rupa sementara.
claims.quote: 「金剛蔵王」とは究極不滅の真理を体現し、あらゆるものを司る王という意。 ... 権現とは「権（かり）の姿で現れた神仏」の意。

claims.statement: In the medieval period Susanoo, the enshrined deity of Izumo Taisha, was regarded as the same being as Zaō Gongen, the principal image of Gakuen-ji.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad pertengahan, Susanoo, dewa Izumo Taisha, dianggap satu wujud dengan Zaō Gongen, dewa utama Gakuenji.
claims.quote: 上記の5組の神々らを祭神とするようになった。 また、中世出雲大社の祭神スサノオが鰐淵寺の本尊蔵王権現と同体とされていた。

claims.statement: The Zaō range on the border of Miyagi and Yamagata prefectures, formerly called Kattamine or Wasurezu no Yama, came to be called Mt. Zaō after Zaō Gongen was invited from Yoshino and ascetics trained there in the Heian period.
claims.statement_id: Pegunungan Zaō di perbatasan Prefektur Miyagi dan Yamagata, dahulu bernama Kattamine atau Wasurezu no Yama, disebut Gunung Zaō karena Zaō Gongen dipindahkan dari Yoshino dan para pertapa berlatih di sana pada zaman Heian.
claims.quote: 宮城県と山形県との県境にある日本百名山の蔵王連峰（蔵王山）は、古くは刈田嶺（かったみね、かったね、かりだのみね）、または、不忘山（わすれずのやま）と呼ばれていた山岳信仰および歌枕の山であったが、吉野から蔵王権現が勧請され、平安時代には修験者が修行するようになったため蔵王山とも呼ばれるようになったとされる。

claims.statement: Amanomichine is an ancestral figure associated with the first Kii provincial ruler.
claims.statement_id: Amanomichine adalah sosok leluhur yang dikaitkan dengan penguasa provinsi Kii pertama.
claims.quote: 天道根命（あまのみちねのみこと/あめの-、生没年不詳）は、古代日本の豪族で初代紀国造。

claims.statement: According to the Sendai Kuji Hongi he is one of the 32 deities escorting Nigihayahi, and the Kokuzō Shidai transmitted by the Kii kuni no miyatsuko family says Emperor Jinmu appointed him first Kii kuni no miyatsuko.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Sendai Kuji Hongi, ia salah satu dari 32 dewa pengawal Nigihayahi, dan Kokuzō Shidai yang diwariskan keluarga kuni no miyatsuko Kii menyebut Kaisar Jinmu mengangkatnya sebagai kuni no miyatsuko Kii pertama.
claims.quote: 『先代旧事本紀』天神本紀によれば高天原から葦原中国へ降臨する事となった饒速日尊の護衛として付き従った32神の1柱で、同書国造本紀や紀伊国造家が伝える『国造次第』によれば神武天皇によって初代の紀伊国造に任じられた。

claims.statement: One genealogical record names Hikoma as his child.
claims.statement_id: Satu catatan silsilah menyebut Hikoma sebagai anaknya.
claims.quote: 紀国造の末裔の紀俊行氏が所有する「紀伊国造次第」では、子に比古麻命がいるとされる。

claims.statement: Genealogical accounts differ over his relationship to Kamimusubi.
claims.statement_id: Catatan silsilah berbeda mengenai hubungannya dengan Kamimusubi.
claims.quote: 「天御食持命の次」の「次」をどのように解するかに問題があり、これを弟と見て神皇産霊尊の子神とすることもできるが、5世の孫とする所伝の方が多い。

claims.statement: According to the Nihonjinmei Daijiten, he is a deity who appears in the Kuji Hongi and a descendant of Kamimusubi.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Nihonjinmei Daijiten, ia adalah dewa yang muncul dalam Kuji Hongi dan keturunan Kamimusubi.
claims.quote: 「旧事本紀(くじほんぎ)」にみえる神。 神皇産霊尊(かみむすびのみこと)の子孫。

claims.statement: According to the same dictionary, he is one of the thirty-two deities sent down from heaven as guards at the descent of the heavenly grandchild, became kuni no miyatsuko of Kii in the time of Emperor Jinmu, and is ancestral deity of the Ki and Kawase clans.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus yang sama, ia salah satu dari tiga puluh dua dewa yang diturunkan dari langit sebagai pengawal pada turunnya cucu langit, menjadi kuni no miyatsuko Kii pada masa Kaisar Jinmu, dan leluhur klan Ki dan Kawase.
claims.quote: 天孫降臨の際,警護のため天からくだされた三十二神の一神。神武天皇のときに紀伊国造(きのくにのみやつこ)となったという。紀氏,川瀬氏らの祖先神。

claims.statement: According to the Shinsen Shōjiroku, he is a fifth-generation descendant of Kamimusubi (the same as Kamimusubi no Mikoto), and is said to be ancestor of several clans such as Shigeno, Ōsaka, Ki and Kawase.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Shinsen Shōjiroku, ia cicit keempat Kamimusubi (disebut juga Kamimusubi), dan dikatakan leluhur sejumlah klan seperti Shigeno, Ōsaka, Ki, dan Kawase.
claims.quote: 『新撰姓氏録』では神魂命（神皇産霊尊に同じ）の5世の孫で、滋野宿祢、大坂直、紀直、大村直田連、川瀬造、また伊蘇氏（伊蘇志）・楢原氏・滋野氏の祖と伝わる。

claims.statement: According to a variant in the "Kokuzō-ke fu" recorded in the Kii Zoku Fudoki, he followed the descent of Hinokuma no Ōkami and Kunikakasu no Ōkami and served them, then during Emperor Jinmu's eastern expedition brought the two sacred treasures, the sun-image mirror and the sun spear, to Nagusa District in Kii Province, enshrined them at Kotonoura in Kemi, and prayed for the emperor's success; the Hinokuma shrine stands at Akizuki, Wakayama City, and Kemi is now part of Wakayama.
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi lain dalam "Kokuzō-ke fu" yang dimuat Kii Zoku Fudoki, ia mengiringi turunnya Hinokuma no Ōkami dan Kunikakasu no Ōkami dan melayani mereka, lalu pada penaklukan timur Kaisar Jinmu membawa dua pusaka, cermin Hinokata dan tombak Hinoboko, ke Distrik Nagusa, Provinsi Kii, memantapkannya di Kotonoura di Kemi, dan berdoa bagi keberhasilan sang kaisar; Hinokuma-gu terletak di Akizuki, Kota Wakayama, dan Kemi kini termasuk Wakayama.
claims.quote: 異伝として『紀伊続風土記』所載の「国造家譜」は、日前大神と国懸大神（紀伊国造が奉斎する和歌山県和歌山市秋月鎮座の日前宮の祭神）の降臨に随従して以後両大神に仕え、後に神武天皇の東征に際して両大神の神体である日像鏡と日矛の2種の神宝を奉戴して紀伊国名草郡に到来し、毛見郷（現和歌山市毛見）の琴ノ浦にそれを鎮座させて天皇の東征の成功を祈念した

claims.statement: According to the Kii Kokuzō Keizu, when Amaterasu hid in the heavenly rock cave the gods of Takamagahara entrusted Amenomichine with two sacred treasures, a sun-image mirror and a sun spear cast by Ishikoridome, and he venerated them as Amaterasu's "Sakinomitama".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kii Kokuzō Keizu, ketika Amaterasu bersembunyi di gua langit, para dewa Takamagahara menitipkan kepada Amenomichine dua pusaka, cermin matahari dan tombak matahari yang dituang oleh Ishikoridome, dan ia memujanya sebagai "Sakinomitama" Amaterasu.
claims.quote: 天道根命は天照大神の天岩戸隠れに際して石凝姥命によって鋳造された日像鏡と日矛の2種の神宝を高天原の神々から託され、高天原においてこれを天照大神の「前霊（さきのみたま）」として奉斎していたが

claims.statement: According to that genealogy, he married Jidōme, daughter of a local deity, and had Hikoma, whose descendants served the Hinokuma and Kunikakasu shrines; it ends by calling him a "long-lived deity" who lived from the time of Kamimusubi to the reign of Emperor Jinmu.
claims.statement_id: Menurut silsilah itu, ia menikahi Jidōme, putri dewa setempat, dan memiliki putra Hikoma yang keturunannya melayani kuil Hinokuma dan Kunikakasu; ia berakhir sebagai "dewa berumur panjang" yang hidup dari zaman Kamimusubi hingga masa Kaisar Jinmu.
claims.quote: 現地の神の女である地道女命を娶って比古麻命を儲け、以来その子孫が国造として日前・国懸両神宮を奉斎するよう受け継いだといい、最後に「神皇産霊尊の時より神武天皇の御宇に至る」まで在世した「長寿の神」であったと結ばれている。

claims.statement: On Amenomichine's descent, some say he followed the two great kami Hinokuma and Kunikakasu, others the "descent of the heavenly grandchild", and for the latter views divide on whether the principal was Ninigi or Nigihayahi.
claims.statement_id: Tentang turunnya Amenomichine, ada yang menyebut ia mengiringi dua dewa besar Hinokuma dan Kunikakasu, ada yang menyebut ia mengiringi "turunnya cucu langit", dan yang terakhir terbagi apakah tokoh utamanya Ninigi atau Nigihayahi.
claims.quote: 天道根命の降臨について、日前・国懸両大神に随従したものと説くものと、「天孫降臨」に随従するものとであったと説くものに分かれるが、更に後者については降臨の主体を天津彦彦火瓊瓊杵尊とするか饒速日尊とするかで説が分かれる。

claims.statement: The Kii Zoku Fudoki rejects his attendance at the descent of the heavenly grandchild, Jinmu's eastern expedition and the link with Hinokuma-gu as erroneous tradition, and suggests that in Kii Amenomichine enshrined the three Itakiso deities rather than the two treasures.
claims.statement_id: Kii Zoku Fudoki menolak pengiringan pada turunnya cucu langit, penaklukan timur Jinmu, dan hubungan dengan Hinokuma-gu sebagai kabar keliru, dan menduga Amenomichine di Kii memuja tiga dewa Itakiso, bukan dua pusaka.
claims.quote: また『紀伊続風土記』は、天孫降臨での供奉や神武天皇の東征、日前宮との関係等は全て誤伝であると斥け、『先代旧事本紀』地祇本紀に紀伊国造は五十猛命、大屋姫命、抓津姫命の所謂伊太祁曽三神を祀ると伝わるので、天道根命自体は紀伊において2種の神宝ではなくこの3神を祀っていたものであろうと説いている。

claims.statement: Many writers regard the appointment as kuni no miyatsuko told of the time of Emperor Jinmu, together with the other provincial governors in the Kokuzō Hongi, as a tradition hard to believe.
claims.statement_id: Banyak penulis menilai pengangkatan sebagai kuni no miyatsuko pada masa Kaisar Jinmu, seperti kuni no miyatsuko lain dalam Kokuzō Hongi, sebagai tradisi yang sulit dipercaya.
claims.quote: 従って初代の神武天皇朝に掛けて語られる国造就任は『先代旧事本紀』「国造本紀」に見える諸国の国造とともに信じ難い所伝であるとする論者が多い。

claims.statement: The Sendai Kuji Hongi places him "next" after Amenomimochi, a child of Kamimusubi, and makes him ancestor of the Kawase no Miyatsuko and others (Jindai Hongi, Kokuzō Hongi).
claims.statement_id: Menurut Sendai Kuji Hongi, ia "berikutnya" setelah Amenomimochi, putra Kamimusubi, dan leluhur Kawase no Miyatsuko dan lainnya (Jindai Hongi, Kokuzō Hongi).
claims.quote: 『先代旧事本紀』は神皇産霊尊の子神である天御食持命の「次」で、川（河）瀬造などの祖とするが（神代本紀・国造本紀）

claims.statement: The black dragon is a dragon figure in European and East Asian traditions.
claims.statement_id: Naga hitam adalah sosok naga dalam tradisi Eropa dan Asia Timur.
claims.quote: 黒竜（旧字体: 黑龍󠄂、こくりゅう、拼音: hēilóng ヘイロン）は、ヨーロッパや中国や日本の伝承および物語、神話に登場する竜の一種。

claims.statement: In five-phase thought it is associated with water and the north.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pemikiran lima unsur ia dikaitkan dengan air dan utara.
claims.quote: 五行思想においては、黒は北と同じく水に対応するので、黒竜を玄武と同様、「北方を守護する神聖な竜」としている。

claims.statement: It is interpreted as a sacred guardian of the north.
claims.statement_id: Ia ditafsirkan sebagai penjaga suci utara.
claims.quote: 五行思想においては、黒は北と同じく水に対応するので、黒竜を玄武と同様、「北方を守護する神聖な竜」としている。

claims.statement: Its depictions often give an eastern dragon black scales and two forelegs.
claims.statement_id: Gambarnya sering memberi naga timur sisik hitam dan dua kaki depan.
claims.quote: 名前通り全身の鱗が黒く、前足が2本しかない東洋の竜として描かれる事が多い。驪竜（りりょう）とも呼ばれ、これは顎の下に貴重な珠を持っているともされる 。

claims.statement: In some regions the black dragon is worshipped as a sacred being, like other dragons.
claims.statement_id: Di sebagian daerah, naga hitam dihormati sebagai makhluk suci seperti naga-naga lain.
claims.quote: よって、一部の地域では、黒竜を他の竜同様に、神聖な存在として祀っている。

claims.statement: In the Huainanzi, Nüwa (女媧) slew a black dragon (黑龍) to save Jizhou (冀州), and piled up reed ashes to stop the flood waters.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Huainanzi, Nüwa (女媧) membunuh naga hitam (黑龍) untuk menyelamatkan Jizhou (冀州) dan menimbun abu alang-alang untuk menghentikan banjir.
claims.quote: 於是女媧煉五色石以補蒼天，斷鼇足以立四極。殺黑龍以濟冀州，積蘆灰以止淫水。

claims.statement: Takaokami no Ōkami (高龗大神) is sometimes identified as Kokuryū Daimyōjin (黒龍大明神, "Great Deity Black Dragon").
claims.statement_id: Takaokami no Ōkami (高龗大神) kadang disebut Kokuryū Daimyōjin (黒龍大明神).
claims.quote: また高龗大神（たかおかみ）のことを黒龍大明神とすることもある。

claims.statement: At Hōgon-ji on Chikubu Island, the black dragon is enshrined as one of the Eight Dragon Kings in the Kokuryū-dō (Black Dragon Hall).
claims.statement_id: Di Hōgon-ji di Pulau Chikubu, naga hitam dipuja sebagai salah satu dari Delapan Raja Naga di Kokuryū-dō.
claims.quote: 竹生島の宝厳寺境内にある黒龍堂（黒龍大神・黒龍姫大神）に八大龍王の一尊である黒龍として祀られている。

issues.message: Pernyataan hampir tidak berbagi kata dengan kutipannya sendiri. Pastikan kutipan ini benar-benar mendukung pernyataan ini (bukan kutipan milik klaim lain).

claims.statement: Byōbunozoki is a yōkai in Sekien’s illustrated collection.
claims.statement_id: Byōbunozoki adalah yōkai dalam kumpulan ilustrasi Sekien.
claims.quote: Byōbunozoki (屛(びょうぶ)風(の)闚(ぞき), folding screen peeper) is a Japanese monster in the collection of monster paintings by Toriyama Sekien, "Konjaku Hyakki Shūi".

claims.statement: One account describes a spirit emerging from folding screens.
claims.statement_id: Satu kisah menggambarkan roh yang muncul dari sekat lipat.
claims.quote: Byōbu nozoki is a depraved spirit which emerges from the decorative folding screens known as byōbu .

claims.statement: Its tall, slender body wears white robes.
claims.statement_id: Tubuhnya yang tinggi dan ramping memakai jubah putih.
claims.quote: It’s body is long and lithe, and it wears white robes resembling those of a ghost.

claims.statement: It has long black hair and black teeth.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki rambut hitam panjang dan gigi hitam.
claims.quote: It has long black hair and blackened teeth.

claims.statement: A reference interprets it as an animated screen rather than a human ghost.
claims.statement_id: Rujukan menafsirkannya sebagai sekat hidup, bukan arwah manusia.
claims.quote: Despite the resemblance, byōbu nozoki it is not a yūrei, but is actually the tsukumogami of a folding screen.

claims.statement: That reference attributes its invention to Sekien.
claims.statement_id: Rujukan tersebut mengaitkan penciptaannya dengan Sekien.
claims.quote: Origin : Byōbu nozoki was invented by Toriyama Sekien for his book Konjaku hyakki shūi .

claims.statement: Dōnotsura is a Japanese yōkai depicted in illustrated scrolls.
claims.statement_id: Dōnotsura adalah yōkai Jepang yang digambar dalam gulungan ilustrasi.
claims.quote: 胴面（どうのつら）は、妖怪絵巻に描かれている日本の妖怪。首から上がなく、代わりに胴体に顔がある姿をしている。

claims.statement: Its body lacks a head above the neck.
claims.statement_id: Tubuhnya tidak memiliki kepala di atas leher.
claims.quote: 胴面（どうのつら）は、妖怪絵巻に描かれている日本の妖怪。首から上がなく、代わりに胴体に顔がある姿をしている。

claims.statement: Instead, its face is on its torso.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai gantinya, wajahnya terdapat di badan.
claims.quote: 胴面（どうのつら）は、妖怪絵巻に描かれている日本の妖怪。首から上がなく、代わりに胴体に顔がある姿をしている。

claims.statement: The old scrolls give names and pictures without explanatory text.
claims.statement_id: Gulungan lama memberi nama dan gambar tanpa keterangan.
claims.quote: 尾田郷澄『百鬼夜行絵巻』（1832年）にて、この名称が示されているが江戸時代に描かれた絵巻物には名前と絵があるのみで解説文は一切なく、詳細は不明である。

claims.statement: In the Hyakumonogatari Bake-e Emaki scroll, a yōkai of a similar design is confirmed to be depicted under the name Akahadaka.
claims.statement_id: Dalam gulungan Hyakumonogatari Bake-e Emaki, makhluk dengan rancangan serupa tercatat digambarkan dengan nama Akahadaka.
claims.quote: 詳細は不明である。『百物語化絵絵巻』にも同様のデザインの妖怪があかはだかという名前で描かれていることが確認できる。

claims.statement: Beings with faces on the chest or belly, such as Xingtian, the Blemmyae and Kabandha, are widely distributed across Eurasia, including China, Europe and India.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk berwajah di dada atau perut, seperti Xingtian, Blemmyae, dan Kabandha, tersebar luas di berbagai tempat di Eurasia, termasuk Tiongkok, Eropa, dan India.
claims.quote: 胸や腹にかけて顔のある存在は、刑天、ブレムミュアエ、カバンダなど中国やヨーロッパ・インドをはじめ、ユーラシア大陸各地に広く分布している。

claims.statement: Specifically, Xingtian and similar figures, which came to be drawn in Japan through illustrations of the Shanhaijing, appear to have served as the model for this form.
claims.statement_id: Secara khusus, Xingtian dan sejenisnya, yang kadang digambar di Jepang lewat gambar-gambar Shanhaijing, tampaknya menjadi contoh bagi rupa ini.
claims.quote: 具体的には『山海経』の絵図を通じて日本でも描かれる機会のあった刑天などがその手本となったと見られる。

claims.statement: Dōnotsura's body looks much like a human's except that everything from the neck up is missing; its extremely large facial features are prominently displayed on its torso, as its name implies.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh Dōnotsura tampak mirip manusia, kecuali tidak ada apa pun dari leher ke atas; fitur wajahnya yang sangat besar tampak jelas di batang tubuhnya, sesuai namanya.
claims.quote: Dōnotsura’s body appears much like that of a human’s, except that it is missing everything from the neck up. Its extremely large facial features are prominently displayed on its torso, just as its name implies.

claims.statement: The name Dōnotsura (胴面) is translated as "torso face", with the alternate name akahadaka.
claims.statement_id: Nama Dōnotsura (胴面) diterjemahkan sebagai "wajah batang tubuh", dengan nama lain akahadaka.
claims.quote: Dōnotsura 胴面 どうのつら Translation: torso face Alternate names: akahadaka

claims.statement: According to that source, its most likely origin is a play on words, based on the Japanese expression "dono tsura sagete", used to scold a person who looks inappropriately calm when they should be ashamed of something they have done.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber itu, asal-usulnya kemungkinan besar adalah permainan kata, berdasarkan ungkapan Jepang "dono tsura sagete" yang dipakai untuk menegur orang yang tampak tenang padahal seharusnya malu atas perbuatannya.
claims.quote: However, its most likely origin is as a play on words. There is an expression in Japanese—”dono tsura sagete“—which is used to scold a person who looks inappropriately calm when they should be ashamed of something they’ve done.

claims.statement: Enkō is a kappa-related creature of Hiroshima, Chūgoku and Shikoku.
claims.statement_id: Enkō adalah makhluk terkait kappa dari Hiroshima, Chūgoku, dan Shikoku.
claims.quote: 猿猴（えんこう）は広島県及び中国・四国地方に古くから伝わる伝説上の生き物。河童の一種。

claims.statement: Its hairy form resembles a monkey.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya berbulu dan menyerupai monyet.
claims.quote: 一般的にいう河童と異なるのは、姿が毛むくじゃらで猿に似ている点である。金属を嫌う性質があり、海又は川に住み、泳いでいる人間を襲い、肛門から手を入れて生き胆を抜き取るとされている。

claims.statement: It is said to dislike metal and inhabit sea or river water.
claims.statement_id: Ia konon tidak menyukai logam dan menghuni laut atau sungai.
claims.quote: 一般的にいう河童と異なるのは、姿が毛むくじゃらで猿に似ている点である。金属を嫌う性質があり、海又は川に住み、泳いでいる人間を襲い、肛門から手を入れて生き胆を抜き取るとされている。

claims.statement: A description gives it elastic limbs.
claims.statement_id: Satu gambaran memberinya anggota tubuh yang lentur.
claims.quote: Their long limbs are flexible and elastic, and if you pull on one arm it will stretch while the other arm shrinks.

claims.statement: It has sharp claws on its fingers.
claims.statement_id: Ia memiliki cakar tajam di jarinya.
claims.quote: Their fingers are tipped with sharp claws.

claims.statement: Stories give it disguises as women and dolls.
claims.statement_id: Cerita memberinya penyamaran sebagai perempuan dan boneka.
claims.quote: They are also skilled at transforming and can disguise themselves as human women, dolls, and other forms.

claims.statement: Gangi-kozō is a yōkai depicted in an Edo-period book by Sekien.
claims.statement_id: Gangi-kozō adalah yōkai yang digambar dalam buku zaman Edo karya Sekien.
claims.quote: 岸涯小僧（がんぎこぞう）は、鳥山石燕の江戸時代の妖怪画集『今昔百鬼拾遺』にある妖怪。「岸崖小僧」との表記もある。

claims.statement: The image resembles a hairy kappa.
claims.statement_id: Gambarnya menyerupai kappa berbulu.
claims.quote: 画図には全身が毛に覆われた河童のような妖怪が描かれており、石燕による同書の解説文によれば、やすりのような歯を持ち、川辺で魚を獲るものとされている。

claims.statement: Sekien describes file-like teeth and fishing at riverbanks.
claims.statement_id: Sekien menggambarkan gigi seperti kikir dan kegiatan menangkap ikan di tepi sungai.
claims.quote: 画図には全身が毛に覆われた河童のような妖怪が描かれており、石燕による同書の解説文によれば、やすりのような歯を持ち、川辺で魚を獲るものとされている。

claims.statement: A later description gives it webbed hands and toes.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran belakangan memberinya selaput pada tangan dan jari kaki.
claims.quote: Their most notable features are their webbed hands and toes, and their long teeth which are sharp and jagged like files.

claims.statement: A theory interprets it as a transitional form of kappa.
claims.statement_id: Satu teori menafsirkannya sebagai wujud peralihan kappa.
claims.quote: Some folklorists believe that the gangi kozō is a kind of takiwaro, and thus is merely a transitional form of a kappa.

claims.statement: That account has it generally avoiding people but sometimes meeting fishermen.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu menyebutnya umumnya menghindari manusia tetapi sesekali menemui nelayan.
claims.quote: Gangi kozō normally stay away from people, but occasionally encounter fishermen along the rivers they inhabit.

claims.statement: Gotoku-neko is a cat yōkai in Sekien’s illustrated book.
claims.statement_id: Gotoku-neko adalah yōkai kucing dalam buku bergambar Sekien.
claims.quote: 五徳猫（ごとくねこ）は、鳥山石燕の『百器徒然袋』にある日本の妖怪。

claims.statement: Its image has two tails and a trivet on its head.
claims.statement_id: Gambarnya memiliki dua ekor dan tatakan panci di kepala.
claims.quote: 2本の尻尾を持つ猫が、五徳（囲炉裏で鍋・やかんなどを乗せる台足）を冠のように頭に頂き、火吹き竹を持って囲炉裏で火を起こしている姿で描かれている。

claims.statement: It uses a bamboo tube to stoke a hearth.
claims.statement_id: Ia memakai tabung bambu untuk menyalakan perapian.
claims.quote: 2本の尻尾を持つ猫が、五徳（囲炉裏で鍋・やかんなどを乗せる台足）を冠のように頭に頂き、火吹き竹を持って囲炉裏で火を起こしている姿で描かれている。

claims.statement: A reference classifies it as a type of nekomata.
claims.statement_id: Rujukan menggolongkannya sebagai jenis nekomata.
claims.quote: Appearance : Gotoku neko are a kind of nekomata–large yōkai cats with two tails.

claims.statement: The tips of its twin tails are said to burn like torches.
claims.statement_id: Ujung kedua ekornya konon menyala seperti obor.
claims.quote: The tips of their twin tails burn like torches.

claims.statement: Its name refers to the trivet worn on its head.
claims.statement_id: Namanya merujuk pada tatakan yang dikenakan di kepala.
claims.quote: Its name comes from the gotoku–or trivet–that this yōkai wears like a hat.

claims.statement: Sekien’s commentary mentions the precedent of someone called 五徳の官者 after forgetting two parts of the "seven virtues" dance, and says he wondered in a dream what this cat too might have forgotten; Shinano no Zenji Yukinaga is brought up as a reference.
claims.statement_id: Keterangan Sekien menyebut contoh orang yang dijuluki 五徳の官者 setelah melupakan dua bagian dari tarian "tujuh kebajikan", dan ia bermimpi bertanya-tanya hal apa yang juga dilupakan kucing ini; Shinano no Zenji Yukinaga dijadikan acuan.
claims.quote: 石燕による解説には、「七とくの舞をふたつわすれて五徳の官者と言ひしためしもあればこの猫もいかなることをか忘れけんと夢の中におもひぬ」とあり、信濃前司行長（しなののぜんじ ゆきなが）が引き合いに出されている。

claims.statement: The Tsurezuregusa (section 226) records that Yukinaga was originally a learned man but was nicknamed 五徳の冠者 for forgetting two of the virtues in the "Shichitoku no mai" dance; Sekien’s commentary is seen as a pun between the utensil gotoku (trivet) and 五徳の冠者.
claims.statement_id: Tsurezuregusa (bagian 226) mencatat bahwa Yukinaga pada dasarnya orang berilmu tetapi dijuluki 五徳の冠者 karena melupakan dua dari tujuh kebajikan dalam tarian "Shichitoku no mai"; keterangan Sekien dipandang sebagai permainan kata antara gotoku (tatakan panci) dan 五徳の冠者.
claims.quote: 『徒然草』（第226段）には、行長は本来は学識ある人物だったが、舞曲「七徳の舞」の内の二つの徳を忘れたことから「五徳の冠者」と渾名されたという話が記されている。これは器物の五徳と、五徳の冠者との語呂あわせを石燕がして解説したものであると見られている。

claims.statement: The Muromachi-period Hyakki Yagyō scroll also depicts a creature with a trivet (gotoku) on its head, and Gotoku-neko is thought to have been created by Sekien using that creature’s appearance as a model.
claims.statement_id: Gulungan Hyakki Yagyō zaman Muromachi juga menggambarkan makhluk dengan tatakan panci (gotoku) di kepala, dan Gotoku-neko dianggap diciptakan Sekien dengan meniru rupa makhluk itu.
claims.quote: 室町時代の『百鬼夜行絵巻』にも同様に五徳を頭に乗せた姿の妖怪が描かれており、五徳猫はこの妖怪の姿をモデルにして石燕が創作して描いたものであると考えられている。

claims.statement: According to that source, Gotoku-neko was invented by Toriyama Sekien in his book Hyakki tsurezure bukuro (“An Idle Bag of One Hundred Vessels”).
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber itu, Gotoku-neko diciptakan Toriyama Sekien dalam bukunya Hyakki tsurezure bukuro ("An Idle Bag of One Hundred Vessels").
claims.quote: Gotoku neko was invented by Toriyama Sekien in his book Hyakki tsurezure bukuro (“An Idle Bag of One Hundred Vessels”).

claims.statement: Just as ordinary cats like warmth, gotoku neko are said to hang around fireplaces.
claims.statement_id: Seperti kucing biasa yang menyukai kehangatan, gotoku neko disebut berkeliaran di sekitar perapian.
claims.quote: Just as ordinary cats like warmth, gotoku neko hang around fireplaces.

claims.statement: Hikeshibaba is a yōkai illustrated by Sekien.
claims.statement_id: Hikeshibaba adalah yōkai yang digambar Sekien.
claims.quote: 火消婆（ひけしばば）は、鳥山石燕による江戸時代の妖怪画集『今昔画図続百鬼』にある日本の妖怪。

claims.statement: Its old-woman form blows out household lanterns.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya perempuan tua yang meniup padam lentera rumah.
claims.quote: 人家の中の提灯や行灯などの火を吹き消す、老婆の姿の妖怪。陰気の存在である妖怪は火などの陽気を苦手とするため、その火を消す存在が火消婆だとされる。

claims.statement: A description gives her white hair and a grotesque appearance.
claims.statement_id: Satu gambaran memberinya rambut putih dan penampilan buruk rupa.
claims.quote: Hikeshi baba takes the form of a white-haired, grotesque-looking, old woman.

claims.statement: One account says her actions can cause harm indirectly.
claims.statement_id: Satu kisah menyebut tindakannya dapat mencelakai secara tidak langsung.
claims.quote: Hikeshi baba is not a dangerous yōkai herself, although her actions can indirectly harm people.

claims.statement: That account interprets her work as darkening homes.
claims.statement_id: Kisah tersebut menafsirkan pekerjaannya sebagai menggelapkan rumah.
claims.quote: Her purpose is to make the world a gloomier place by extinguishing the cheerful, beautiful paper lanterns that decorate Japanese homes.

claims.statement: The resulting darkness is described as favorable to other yōkai.
claims.statement_id: Kegelapan yang dihasilkan digambarkan menguntungkan yōkai lain.
claims.quote: Her work is intended to make conditions more suitable for other yōkai to come out and do their own misdeeds.

claims.statement: Hone-karakasa is a yōkai illustrated in Sekien’s book.
claims.statement_id: Hone-karakasa adalah yōkai yang digambar dalam buku Sekien.
claims.quote: 骨傘（ほねからかさ）は、鳥山石燕の『百器徒然袋』に描かれる日本の妖怪である。

claims.statement: Its illustration shows an old paperless umbrella moving through the air in flames.
claims.statement_id: Ilustrasinya menunjukkan payung tua tanpa kertas bergerak di udara dengan api.
claims.quote: 和紙がはがれて骨ばかりとなった古い唐傘（からかさ）が、火をまとって宙を舞う姿で描かれており

claims.statement: A later account interprets it as an animated old paper umbrella.
claims.statement_id: Kisah belakangan menafsirkannya sebagai payung kertas tua yang hidup.
claims.quote: Hone karakasa is a tsukumogami born from an tattered and torn up old Chinese-style paper umbrella.

claims.statement: That account has it dance in the sky on wet and windy days.
claims.statement_id: Kisah itu menyebutnya menari di langit saat hari basah dan berangin.
claims.quote: They spring into life on wet, windy days, and dance through the sky like wild birds.

claims.statement: Its appearance is treated as an omen of bad weather.
claims.statement_id: Kemunculannya dianggap sebagai pertanda cuaca buruk.
claims.quote: Their appearance is a sure sign that bad weather is coming.

claims.statement: It is associated with the umbrella spirit karakasa-kozō.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan roh payung karakasa-kozō.
claims.quote: Hone karakasa are closely related to the much better-known umbrella tsukumogami karakasa-kozō.

claims.statement: Hoyau is a venomous dragon or dragon deity in Ainu tradition.
claims.statement_id: Hoyau adalah naga berbisa atau dewa naga dalam tradisi Ainu.
claims.quote: Hoyau or hoyau kamui (var, oyau kamui), in Ainu mythology, is a type of malodorous and venomous dragon or dragon god, believed to thrive in summer or near fire, but lose strength in the cold, whose trait earns it the alternative name of sak-somo-ayep ("that which must not be mentioned in the summer").

claims.statement: Its habitats include lakes and swamps.
claims.statement_id: Habitatnya meliputi danau dan rawa.
claims.quote: They are generally held to be dwellers of lakes and swamps, but are also winged according to some folklore accounts.

claims.statement: Some accounts give it wings.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian kisah memberinya sayap.
claims.quote: They are generally held to be dwellers of lakes and swamps, but are also winged according to some folklore accounts.

claims.statement: A regional name associates it with western Hidaka.
claims.statement_id: Nama daerah mengaitkannya dengan Hidaka barat.
claims.quote: The sak-somo-ayep is said to dwell in lakes and swamps of the western parts of the Hidaka Subprefecture region.

claims.statement: A Hidaka account describes a stout body with a narrow head and tail.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Hidaka menggambarkan tubuh tebal dengan kepala dan ekor sempit.
claims.quote: According to lore around this Hidaka region, the sak-somo-ayep possesses a winged, serpent-like body, with torso like a tawara or a bale of rice (i.e. stout and cylindrical), and a narrow head and tail emerging out of this trunk.

claims.statement: Its pointed snout is said to cut large trees.
claims.statement_id: Moncongnya yang runcing konon dapat memotong pohon besar.
claims.quote: It also has a pointed, chisel-like snout which can slice or rip large trees.

claims.statement: The sak-somo-ayep not only gives off a foul smell; contact with its body odor makes plants shrivel and die, and humans downwind of the dragon may lose their body hair or develop swellings on the skin.
claims.statement_id: Sak-somo-ayep tidak hanya mengeluarkan bau busuk; kontak dengan bau badannya membuat tumbuhan layu dan mati, dan manusia di arah angin naga itu dapat kehilangan bulu badan atau kulitnya bengkak.
claims.quote: The sak-somo-ayep not only issues a foul smell, but contact with this body odor or musk causes plants to shrivel and die. Humans situated downwind of the dragon may lose their body hair, or develop swells on their skin

claims.statement: According to one epic song (yukar), the dragon-god sak-somo-ayep gave off a stench that was noxious and lethal to both humans and gods, so the deity Okikurmi took on the task of slaying it.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu nyanyian epik (yukar), dewa naga sak-somo-ayep mengeluarkan bau busuk yang beracun dan mematikan bagi manusia dan dewa, sehingga dewa Okikurmi mengambil tugas membunuhnya.
claims.quote: According to one epic song (yukar), the dragon-god sak-somo-ayep issued a stench that was noxious and lethal to both humans and gods, so that the deity Okikurmi took on the task of slaying it.

claims.statement: When the smallpox deity Hōsōshin descended on Abuta (now Tōyako town) and spread smallpox, the people fled to the shore of Lake Tōya, and the hoyau dispelled the Hōsōshin with its horrible stench, saving the townsfolk.
claims.statement_id: Ketika dewa cacar Hōsōshin turun ke Abuta (kini kota Tōyako) dan menyebarkan cacar, orang-orang mengungsi ke tepi Danau Tōya, dan hoyau dengan bau busuknya mengusir Hōsōshin sehingga penduduk selamat.
claims.quote: Specifically, when the Hōsōshin (smallpox deity) descended upon Abuta (now Tōyako town) and caused smallpox to spread, the people fled to the shores of Lake Tōya, and the hoyau with its horrible stench dispelled the Hōsōshin, saving the townsfolk.

claims.statement: Because it abhors the cold, it may spiritually possess a miko (shamaness) and command humans to "stoke the fire".
claims.statement_id: Karena membenci dingin, ia dapat merasuki miko (dukun perempuan) dan memerintahkan manusia untuk "mengobarkan api".
claims.quote: As it abhors the cold, it may spiritually possess a miko (shamaness) and command humans to "stoke the fire".

claims.statement: The Hoyau Kamui of Lake Tōya had the character of a demonic deity, yet at times became a guardian deity of humans.
claims.statement_id: Hoyau Kamui di Danau Tōya berwatak dewa jahat, tetapi kadang menjadi dewa pelindung manusia.
claims.quote: 洞爺湖のホヤウカムイは魔神としての性格を持つ反面、時には人間の守り神となることもあった。疱瘡（天然痘）を司る疫病神であるパヨカカムイが虻田（現・洞爺湖町）に疱瘡を流行させたとき、人々が洞爺湖畔へ逃げてくると、

claims.statement: The Hoyau Kamui of Lake Tōya is also said to look like a winged turtle rather than a serpent deity; during epidemics people offered sake to the mountain spirit of Mt. Usu, Ikeeuseguru, and to Hoyau Kamui, praying for recovery.
claims.statement_id: Hoyau Kamui di Danau Tōya juga dikatakan berwujud seperti kura-kura bersayap, bukan dewa ular; saat wabah, orang mempersembahkan sake kepada roh gunung Usu, Ikeeuseguru, dan Hoyau Kamui untuk berdoa agar penyakit sembuh.
claims.quote: この洞爺湖のホヤウカムイは蛇神ではなく羽の生えた亀のような姿ともいわれ、流行病のあるときには、人々は有珠山の山霊（山の神霊）イケエウセグルとホヤウカムイに酒を捧げ、病気平癒を祈ったと言う。

claims.statement: Hoyau (hoyaw) is said to mean "snake" in the Sakhalin dialect; chatai (catay) is a loanword from Japanese "jatai" ("snake body").
claims.statement_id: Ho yau (hoyaw) dikatakan berarti "ular" dalam dialek Karafuto (Sakhalin); chatai (catay) adalah kata serapan dari bahasa Jepang "jatai" (tubuh ular).
claims.quote: ホヤウ（ホヤゥ / hoyaw "蛇"。樺太方言で"蛇"を意味する言葉とされる） 、チャタイ（チャタィ / catay 日本語の"蛇体"の借用語）

claims.statement: Ame-no-Hiwashi is a deity in Japanese mythology appearing in the Nihon Shoki and the Kogo shūi, ancestor of the Awa Inbe clan who opened up Awa Province, planted fibres and founded spinning work.
claims.statement_id: Ame-no-Hiwashi adalah dewa dalam mitologi Jepang yang muncul dalam Nihon Shoki dan Kogo shūi, leluhur klan Inbe di Awa yang membuka Provinsi Awa, menanam serat, dan merintis pemintalan.
claims.quote: 『日本書紀』や『古語拾遺』に登場する。阿波国を開拓し、穀麻を植えて紡績の業を創始した阿波の忌部氏の祖神。

claims.statement: He is regarded as the ancestor of the Awa Inbe clan.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap sebagai leluhur klan Inbe di Awa.
claims.quote: 『日本書紀』や『古語拾遺』に登場する。阿波国を開拓し、穀麻を植えて紡績の業を創始した阿波の忌部氏の祖神。

claims.statement: A tradition credits him with cultivating fibres and founding spinning work.
claims.statement_id: Satu tradisi menganggapnya menanam bahan serat dan merintis pemintalan.
claims.quote: 『日本書紀』や『古語拾遺』に登場する。阿波国を開拓し、穀麻を植えて紡績の業を創始した阿波の忌部氏の祖神。

claims.statement: He is also called Oe no Kami and Inbe no Kami, and is also regarded as Ame-no-Hiwashikakeruya, a descendant of Takamimusubi or Kamimusubi.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga disebut Oe no Kami dan Inbe no Kami, serta dianggap sebagai Ame-no-Hiwashikakeruya, keturunan Takamimusubi atau Kamimusubi.
claims.quote: 麻植神（おえのかみ）、忌部神（いんべのかみ）とも呼ばれる。また高魂命または神魂命の裔神の天日鷲翔矢命（あめのひわしかけるやのみこと）ともされる。

claims.statement: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, Amenohiwashi (Ame no hiwashi in the Nihongi) is described as the child of Tajikarao and ancestor of the Inbe clan of Awa Province.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Ensiklopedia Shinto, Amenohiwashi (Ame no hiwashi dalam Nihongi) digambarkan sebagai anak Tajikarao dan leluhur klan Inbe di Provinsi Awa.
claims.quote: [Ame no hiwashi] (Nihongi) ... Described as the child of Tajikarao, ancestor of the Inbe clan of Awa Province

claims.statement: This deity is said to have planted paper mulberry trees and produced bark-fiber offerings (nigite) from them at the time of Amaterasu's hiding in the Rock Cave of Heaven and at the Descent of the Heavenly Grandchild.
claims.statement_id: Dewa ini dikatakan menanam pohon murbei kertas dan membuat persembahan serat kulit kayu (nigite) darinya ketika Amaterasu bersembunyi di gua batu surga dan pada turunnya cucu langit.
claims.quote: this deity is said to have planted paper mulberry trees and produced bark-fiber offerings (nigite) from them at the time of Amaterasu's hiding away in the Rock Cave of Heaven, and at the Descent of the Heavenly Grandchild (tenson kōrin).

claims.statement: On the basis of these events, Amenohiwashi is considered an occupational kami with jurisdiction over the production of ritual implements.
claims.statement_id: Atas dasar peristiwa itu, Amenohiwashi dipandang sebagai kami pekerjaan yang berwenang atas pembuatan perkakas ritual.
claims.quote: Based on these events, Amenohiwashi is considered an occupational kami with jurisdiction over the production of ritual implements.

claims.statement: The Kogo shūi also states that Amenohiwashi was a vassal of Futodama no mikoto, ancestral deity of the Inbe clan, who were responsible for court ritual.
claims.statement_id: Kogo shūi juga menyatakan bahwa Amenohiwashi adalah pengikut Futodama, dewa leluhur klan Inbe yang bertanggung jawab atas ritual istana.
claims.quote: Kogo shūi also states that Amenohiwashi was a vassal of Futodama no mikoto, ancestral deity (sojin) of the Inbe clan, who were responsible for court ritual.

claims.statement: The descendants of Amenohiwashi crossed over to Awa Province in Shikoku in search of lands to cultivate grains and hemp, and as a result the Awa Inbe clan developed the tradition of offering hemp and paper-mulberry textiles to the emperor at the accession ceremony or Daijōsai.
claims.statement_id: Keturunan Amenohiwashi menyeberang ke Provinsi Awa di Shikoku mencari tanah untuk menanam biji-bijian dan rami, sehingga klan Inbe Awa mengembangkan tradisi mempersembahkan tekstil rami dan murbei kertas kepada kaisar pada upacara penobatan atau Daijōsai.
claims.quote: The descendants of Amenohiwashi crossed over to Awa Province in Shikoku in search of lands to cultivate grains and hemp. As a result, the Awa Inbe clan developed the tradition of offering hemp and paper-mulberry textiles to the emperor on the occasion of the imperial accession ceremony or Daijōsai.

claims.statement: In the well-known myth, when Amaterasu entered the heavenly rock cave and the gods began to dance, Ame no Hiwashi played a stringed instrument and an eagle perched on the end of the string; the gods rejoiced at it as an auspicious bird, and the character for "eagle" (washi) was added to his name.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitos yang terkenal, saat Amaterasu masuk gua batu surga dan para dewa mulai menari, Ame no Hiwashi memainkan alat musik petik dan seekor elang hinggap di ujung senarnya; para dewa menyukainya sebagai pertanda baik sehingga aksara "elang" (washi) ditambahkan pada namanya.
claims.quote: 神話で知られているのは天照大神が天岩戸に入られたとき、岩戸の前で神々の踊りが始まり、天日鷲神が弦楽器を奏でると、弦の先に鷲が止まった。多くの神々が、これは世の中を明るくする吉祥を表す鳥といって喜ばれ、この神の名として鷲の字を加えて、天日鷲命とされた。

claims.statement: According to the Kogo shūi, he is one of four deities following Futodama; when Amaterasu hid in the rock cave he planted paper mulberry and cotton and made white nigite, so he is also called the "hemp-planting kami" and becomes a kami of spinning and papermaking.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Kogo shūi, ia salah satu dari empat dewa pengikut Futodama; ketika Amaterasu bersembunyi di gua batu, ia menanam kajinoki dan kapas serta membuat nigite putih, sehingga disebut "dewa penanam rami" dan menjadi dewa pemintalan dan pembuatan kertas.
claims.quote: 『古語拾遺』によると、天日鷲神は太玉命に従う四柱の神のうちの1柱である。やはり、天照大神が天岩戸に隠れた際に、穀（カジノキ：楮の一種）・木綿などを植えて白和幣（にきて）を作ったとされる。そのため、天日鷲神は「麻植の神」とも呼ばれ、紡績業・製紙業の神となる。

claims.statement: He is generally known as Otori-sama and is worshipped as a guardian of good catches, commercial and industrial prosperity, good fortune, pioneering and industrial promotion.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikenal luas sebagai Otori-sama dan dipuja sebagai dewa pelindung hasil tangkapan ikan, kemakmuran dagang dan industri, nasib baik, pembukaan lahan, dan peningkatan produksi.
claims.quote: また、天日鷲神は一般にお酉様として知られ、豊漁、商工業繁栄、開運、開拓、殖産の守護神として信仰されている。

claims.statement: At the Daijōsai of an emperor's accession, the Miki family, regarded as descendants of the Awa Inbe, prepares the aratae cloth from hemp they grow.
claims.statement_id: Pada Daijōsai penobatan kaisar, keluarga Miki, yang dianggap keturunan Inbe Awa, menyiapkan aratae dari rami yang mereka tanam.
claims.quote: 天皇即位の大嘗祭に際して、阿波忌部の末裔とされる三木家が育てた麻を元に、麁服（あらたえ）を調進している。

claims.statement: Other names include Ame no Hiwashi no Mikoto, Amenohiwashikakeruya and Hiwashi no Mikoto; other designations are Oe no Kami and Inbe no Kami.
claims.statement_id: Nama lain mencakup Ame no Hiwashi no Mikoto, Amenohiwashikakeruya, dan Hiwashi no Mikoto; sebutan lain adalah Oe no Kami dan Inbe no Kami.
claims.quote: 別名 天日鷲命、天日鷲翔矢命、天毘和志可気流夜命、日鷲命、天日和志命、天比和志命など 別称 麻植神、忌部神

claims.statement: He is enshrined as principal deity at Washi Shrine in Senzoku, Taito Ward, Tokyo, and at Inbe Shrine in Nikenya-chō, Tokushima City.
claims.statement_id: Ia dipuja sebagai dewa utama di Washi Jinja di Senzoku, Distrik Taito, Tokyo, dan di Inbe Jinja di Nikenya-chō, Kota Tokushima.
claims.quote: 鷲神社（東京都台東区千束） - 主祭神 忌部神社（徳島県徳島市二軒屋町） - 主祭神。

claims.statement: Ame-no-Mahitotsu is a Japanese deity of ironworking and smithing.
claims.statement_id: Ame-no-Mahitotsu adalah dewa Jepang dalam pengolahan besi dan penempaan.
claims.quote: 天目一箇神（あめのまひとつのかみ）は、日本神話に登場する製鉄・鍛冶の神。

claims.statement: The deity appears in several classical chronicles and provincial records.
claims.statement_id: Dewa itu muncul dalam beberapa kronik klasik dan catatan provinsi.
claims.quote: 『古語拾遺』、『日本書紀』、『播磨国風土記』に登場する。別名は天之麻比止都禰命（あめのまひとつねのみこと）、

claims.statement: The Shinsen Shōjiroku calls him the child of Amatsuhikone.
claims.statement_id: Shinsen Shōjiroku menyebutnya anak Amatsuhikone.
claims.quote: 『新撰姓氏録』によれば、天目一箇神は天津彦根命の子である。後裔には、筑紫国・伊勢国の忌部氏、山城国菅田首、山城国山背忌寸、大和国葦田首、山代直（山背国造）がいる。

claims.statement: Amatsumara is among the names associated with this deity.
claims.statement_id: Amatsumara termasuk nama yang dikaitkan dengan dewa ini.
claims.quote: 別名は天之麻比止都禰命（あめのまひとつねのみこと）、天久斯麻比止都命（あめのくしまひとつのみこと）、天津麻羅（あまつまら）、

claims.statement: The Kogo shūi states that at the time of Amaterasu's hiding in the rock cave of heaven, Amenomahitotsu no kami ("the one-eyed kami of heaven") was assigned to make metal weapons.
claims.statement_id: Kogo shūi menyebut bahwa pada saat Amaterasu bersembunyi di gua batu surga, Amenomahitotsu no kami ("kami bermata satu dari surga") ditugaskan membuat senjata logam.
claims.quote: Kogo shūi describes Amatsumara as a follower of Futodama; it also states that at the time of Amaterasu's hiding away in the rock cave of heaven, Amenomahitotsu no kami ("the one-eyed kami of heaven") was assigned to make metal weapons

claims.statement: During the reign of Emperor Sujin, that kami's descendants, together with the descendants of Ishikoridome, were put in charge of recasting the divine mirror and sword.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa pemerintahan Kaisar Sujin, keturunan kami itu bersama keturunan Ishikoridome ditugaskan menempa ulang cermin dan pedang suci.
claims.quote: during the reign of Emperor Sujin, the descendants of that kami were, together with the descendants of Ishikoridome, put in charge of recasting the divine mirror and sword.

claims.statement: According to an "alternate writing" in the Nihongi, Takamimusuhi designated Amenomahitotsu as a metalworker to serve the kami of Izumo.
claims.statement_id: Menurut "tulisan alternatif" dalam Nihongi, Amenomahitotsu ditunjuk oleh Takamimusuhi sebagai pandai logam untuk melayani kami Izumo.
claims.quote: According to an "alternate writing" included in Nihongi, Amenomahitotsu was designated by Takamimusuhi as a metalworker to serve the kami of Izumo.

claims.statement: From these incidents, Amenomahitotsu is recognized as the same kami as Amatsumara.
claims.statement_id: Dari kejadian-kejadian tersebut, Amenomahitotsu diakui sebagai kami yang sama dengan Amatsumara.
claims.quote: From these incidents, Amenomahitotsu is recognized as the same kami as Amatsumara.

claims.statement: The Kojiki states that Amatsumara, as the blacksmith of the Plain of High Heaven, was called upon to refine the iron used for making mirrors.
claims.statement_id: Kojiki menyatakan bahwa Amatsumara, sebagai pandai besi di Dataran Tinggi Surga, dipanggil untuk menempa besi yang dipakai membuat cermin.
claims.quote: Kojiki states that as the blacksmith of the Plain of High Heaven, Amatsumara was called upon to refine the iron used for making mirrors

claims.statement: Together with Ishikoridome, he was said to have assisted in making the mirror used to lure Amaterasu out of her hiding place in the rock cave of heaven.
claims.statement_id: Bersama Ishikoridome, ia dikatakan membantu membuat cermin yang dipakai untuk memancing Amaterasu keluar dari tempat persembunyiannya di gua batu surga.
claims.quote: Together with Ishikoridome, he was said to have assisted in the making of the mirror used to lure Amaterasu from her hiding place in the rock cave of heaven.

claims.statement: Azukibabaa is a yōkai associated with Miyagi.
claims.statement_id: Azukibabaa adalah yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan Miyagi.
claims.quote: Azukibabaa (あずきばばあ, "the bean hag") is a monster (known in Japanese as a yōkai) from Miyagi Prefecture in the Kanto region of Japan.

claims.statement: It takes an old woman’s form and makes bean-like sounds.
claims.statement_id: Wujudnya perempuan tua yang membuat bunyi seperti kacang.
claims.quote: It is said to be an old woman who produces a sound similar to that made by azuki beans, which is referred to as azukiarai.

claims.statement: A local story places the sound at an abandoned temple on rainy evenings.
claims.statement_id: Cerita setempat menempatkan bunyinya di kuil terbengkalai pada petang hujan.
claims.quote: Kawagoe City, Saitama Prefecture It is said that at the abandoned temple in Shimo-Kosaka-mura, the sound of azuki beans can be heard on a rainy evening.

claims.statement: Parents invoke the figure to warn disobedient children.
claims.statement_id: Orang tua menyebut sosok itu untuk memperingatkan anak yang tidak patuh.
claims.quote: In this region, parents told disobedient children that they would be "attacked by the old woman bean smasher".

claims.statement: In Gunma Prefecture, at a stream near Takasaki Castle, at night it produces the sound of azuki beans while singing an offer to wash or eat the red beans, and swallows passersby.
claims.statement_id: Di Prefektur Gunma, di sebuah sungai dekat Kastil Takasaki, pada malam hari ia membuat bunyi kacang azuki sambil menyanyikan tawaran mencuci atau memakan kacang merah, dan menelan orang yang lewat.
claims.quote: Gunma Prefecture the yōkai appears in a stream near Takasaki Castle. At night, it produces the sound of azuki beans while singing "Would you like to wash or eat the red beans?" and swallows passersby.

claims.statement: Another location associates it with sounds from a swamp.
claims.statement_id: Lokasi lain mengaitkannya dengan bunyi dari rawa.
claims.quote: In Showa-mura, it makes the sound of stirring azuki beans in a pot in a swamp.

claims.statement: According to Yokai.com, in Miyagi Prefecture this yōkai takes the form of a fearsome old hag dressed all in white, singing in a husky, ugly voice.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Yokai.com, di Prefektur Miyagi yōkai ini berupa perempuan tua yang menakutkan, berpakaian serba putih, dan bernyanyi dengan suara serak yang buruk.
claims.quote: The people of Miyagi Prefecture tell of a much more sinister member of the azuki family of yōkai. Rather than the benign and cute azuki arai known throughout the country, this northeastern variation takes the form of a fearsome old hag dressed all in white, singing in a husky, ugly voice.

claims.statement: Azuki babā appear only at twilight, particularly on rainy or misty autumn nights.
claims.statement_id: Azuki babā hanya muncul saat senja, terutama pada malam musim gugur yang berhujan atau berkabut.
claims.quote: Azuki babā appear only at twilight—particularly on rainy or misty autumn nights.

claims.statement: Witnesses describe an eerie white glow visible through a thick white mist; from the mist comes the husky voice of an old hag singing her song and counting beans as she washes them in the river with a strainer, and those who do not turn away at this point never make it back.
claims.statement_id: Para saksi menggambarkan cahaya putih yang menyeramkan tampak di balik kabut tebal; dari kabut terdengar suara serak perempuan tua yang menyanyikan lagunya sambil menghitung kacang yang ia cuci di sungai dengan saringan, dan yang tidak berpaling saat itu tidak pernah kembali.
claims.quote: Witnesses of azuki babā describe an eerie, white glow visible through a thick, white mist. ... counting beans as she washes them in the river with a strainer. ... Those who don’t turn away at this point never make it back.

claims.statement: Their song is similar to the azuki arai's, except that azuki babā follow through on the threat to catch and eat humans.
claims.statement_id: Lagunya mirip lagu azuki arai, tetapi azuki babā benar-benar menangkap dan memakan manusia.
claims.quote: Their song is similar to the azuki arai’s, except that azuki babā follow through on the threat to catch and eat humans.

claims.statement: Despite their ferociousness they are mostly found only in stories used to scare children into behaving properly; of all azuki-related yōkai variations this one is the most likely to be a shape-shifted evil itachi, tanuki or kitsune imitating the azuki arai to catch and eat a child.
claims.statement_id: Meskipun garang, ia kebanyakan hanya ditemukan dalam cerita untuk menakut-nakuti anak agar berperilaku baik; di antara varian yōkai terkait azuki, inilah yang paling mungkin merupakan itachi, tanuki, atau kitsune jahat yang berubah wujud menirukan azuki arai untuk memikat anak.
claims.quote: Despite their ferociousness, they are mostly found only in stories used to scare children into behaving properly. ... this one is the most likely to be a shape-shifted evil itachi, tanuki, or kitsune imitating the harmless azuki arai to attract a curious child to catch and eat.

claims.statement: According to Digital Daijisen Plus, it is a Japanese yōkai in the form of an old woman who makes the sound of washing azuki beans, told mainly around Kawagoe in Saitama Prefecture and the Kantō region, and regarded as the same kind as azuki arai.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Digital Daijisen Plus, ia adalah yōkai Jepang berwujud nenek yang membuat bunyi mencuci kacang azuki, dikisahkan terutama di Kawagoe, Prefektur Saitama, dan sekitar wilayah Kantō, serta dianggap sejenis dengan azuki arai.
claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。小豆をとぐ音をたてる老婆の姿をしたもので、埼玉県川越市など関東地方の中心に伝わる。小豆洗いと同種のものとされる。

claims.statement: In Showa-mura it makes the sound of stirring azuki beans in a pot in a swamp; it is said to be mujina or itachi.
claims.statement_id: Di Showa-mura, ia membuat bunyi mengaduk kacang azuki dalam panci di rawa; dikatakan ia adalah mujina atau itachi.
claims.quote: In Showa-mura, it makes the sound of stirring azuki beans in a pot in a swamp. It is said to be mujina or itachi.

claims.statement: At Nakamaru Kakigihira, Kiyoharu Village, Kita-Koma District, Yamanashi Prefecture, Azukibabaa lives in a large tree near Suwa Shrine and calls out to people passing at night, "Eat some azuki beans"; if the person is surprised and confused, she scoops them up into the tree with a large basket.
claims.statement_id: Di Nakamaru Kakigihira, Desa Kiyoharu, Distrik Kita-Koma, Prefektur Yamanashi, Azukibabaa tinggal di pohon besar dekat Kuil Suwa dan memanggil orang yang lewat malam hari, "Makanlah kacang azuki"; bila orang itu terkejut dan bingung, ia menyendoknya ke atas pohon dengan keranjang besar.
claims.quote: Nakamaru Kakigihira, Kiyoharu Village, Kita-Koma District, Yamanashi Prefecture A local yōkai is also known as Azukibabaa. She lives in a large tree near Suwa Shrine and calls out to people who pass by at night, saying, "Eat some azuki beans", and if the person is surprised and confused, she will scoop them up into the tree with a large basket.

claims.statement: The yōkai mythologist Kenji Murakami believes she is related to the Tsurube-otoshi yōkai, which is also said to scoop people up from the tops of trees.
claims.statement_id: Pakar yōkai Murakami Kenji berpendapat ia berkaitan dengan Tsurube-otoshi, yōkai yang juga dikatakan menyendok orang dari puncak pohon.
claims.quote: Yōkai mythologist Kenji Murakami believes she is related to the Tsurube-otoshi yōkai, which is also said to scoop people up from the tops of trees.

claims.statement: In Kawawa Town, Tsuzuki Ward, Yokohama, Kanagawa Prefecture, as in Saitama, she is spoken of as the "old woman polishing azuki beans", a child-threatening monster.
claims.statement_id: Di Kota Kawawa, Distrik Tsuzuki, Yokohama, Prefektur Kanagawa, seperti di Saitama, ia disebut "nenek penggosok kacang azuki", monster yang dipakai menakuti anak.
claims.quote: Kawawa Town, Tsuzuki Ward, Yokohama City, Kanagawa Prefecture Similarly as in Saitama, Azukibabaa is spoken of as the "old woman polishing azuki beans", a child-threatening monster.

claims.statement: At Nishi Narita, Tomiya City, Miyagi Prefecture, a local yōkai called the "Azukiarai Old Woman" appears as an old woman in a stream at dusk; her true form is said to be a kitsune.
claims.statement_id: Di Nishi Narita, Kota Tomiya, Prefektur Miyagi, yōkai setempat disebut "nenek Azukiarai" yang muncul sebagai perempuan tua di sungai saat senja; wujud sejatinya dikatakan kitsune.
claims.quote: Nishi Narita, Tomiya City, Miyagi Prefecture A local yōkai is called the "Azukiarai Old Woman" and appears in the form of an old woman in a stream at dusk. It is said that her true form is a kitsune.

claims.statement: Azukihakari is a sound-producing yōkai in an Edo-period tale collection.
claims.statement_id: Azukihakari adalah yōkai pembuat bunyi dalam kumpulan cerita zaman Edo.
claims.quote: Azukihakari (小豆はかり; "the bean counter") is a Japanese monster in the Ghost Story Collection of the Edo period, "Kaidan Old Staff".

claims.statement: Its unseen bean sounds have been compared to a poltergeist.
claims.statement_id: Bunyi kacangnya yang tidak terlihat disamakan dengan poltergeist.
claims.quote: There is a theory that it is similar to the poltergeist phenomenon because it is a monster that makes the sound of red beans in a house without appearing, and it is a monster with only sound.

claims.statement: A visiting man stays at a house to investigate the phenomenon.
claims.statement_id: Seorang tamu menginap di rumah untuk memeriksa fenomena itu.
claims.quote: The man said: "I want to see it" and stayed at said friend's house.

claims.statement: He hears movement above the ceiling followed by scattering-bean sounds.
claims.statement_id: Ia mendengar gerakan di atas langit-langit lalu bunyi kacang berhamburan.
claims.quote: As mentioned above, when the room was quiet, there was a loud noise as if stepping over the ceiling, followed by the sound of sowing beans.

claims.statement: Later sounds come from the garden.
claims.statement_id: Bunyi berikutnya berasal dari kebun.
claims.quote: Eventually, the sounds of clogging and watering came from the garden outside of the house, rather than from the ceiling.

claims.statement: The man opened the shoji (sliding door) immediately, but no one was in the garden.
claims.statement_id: Pria itu segera membuka shoji (pintu geser), tetapi tidak ada seorang pun di kebun.
claims.quote: The man opened the shoji immediately but said no one was in the garden.

claims.statement: The azuki hakari is a poltergeist found in some homes and temples, known only by the sounds it makes; it is said to dwell in attics or gardens and to be most active at night.
claims.statement_id: Azuki hakari adalah poltergeist yang ditemukan di sebagian rumah dan kuil, hanya dikenal lewat bunyi yang mereka timbulkan; konon mereka tinggal di loteng atau kebun dan paling aktif pada malam hari.
claims.quote: A poltergeist found in some homes and temples, these yōkai are known only by the sounds they make. They are said to dwell in attics or gardens, and are most active at night.

claims.statement: The azuki hakari has never been seen directly, only heard.
claims.statement_id: Azuki hakari tidak pernah terlihat langsung, hanya terdengar.
claims.quote: Azuki hakari have never been seen directly—only heard.

claims.statement: The sound grows progressively louder, gradually turning into the sound of splashing water and finally the sound of geta (Japanese wooden sandals) walking just outside the room.
claims.statement_id: Bunyinya makin keras, perlahan berubah menjadi bunyi air memercik, lalu akhirnya bunyi geta (sandal kayu Jepang) yang berjalan tepat di luar ruangan.
claims.quote: The sound grows progressively louder, and gradually changes into the sound of splashing water, then finally to the sound of geta—Japanese wooden sandals—walking just outside the room.

claims.statement: Opening the doors or windows makes the noise stop, revealing no sign of any creature.
claims.statement_id: Membuka pintu atau jendela menghentikan bunyi itu, dan tidak tampak tanda makhluk apa pun.
claims.quote: Opening the doors or windows causes the noise to stop, revealing no sign of any creature
